can_answer: partly: this measures the annual number of pedestrian casualties in reported Brooklyn crashes, but cannot establish per-pedestrian risk or all aspects of road safety
metric: Annual pedestrian casualties, defined as reported pedestrian injuries plus reported pedestrian deaths
denominator: No denominator; an annual count summed across qualifying crash rows
population: Police-reported Brooklyn crashes in the years counted, with reported pedestrian injury/death counts attributed to each crash
years: Complete calendar years 2013 through 2025; exclude 2026 because coverage ends 2026-06-11
data_check_findings: Across final plan years 2013–2025, 659,713 of 2,132,218 city crash rows (30.9%) have a missing or unknown borough; these cannot be assigned to Brooklyn and are excluded. There are zero impossible borough values, zero null crash dates, and zero missing pedestrian injury/death values among Brooklyn rows in 2013–2025. 2026 is partial (2026-01-01 through 2026-06-11), so it is excluded; 2013–2025 are full calendar years.
data_check_decisions: Exclude rows without a usable Brooklyn borough assignment rather than assigning unknown locations to Brooklyn; exclude the partial 2026 year; retain all valid Brooklyn rows because the two summed outcome fields have no missing values.
limitations: This is a count of reported pedestrian casualties, not a pedestrian-exposure-adjusted risk measure; unlocated crashes are omitted, and 2026 is excluded as partial. The data does not establish all dimensions of road safety.
